titles: The Biggest Living Thing on Earth Isn't a Whale
A Single Plant Twice the Size of Paris (Shown to Scale)
hook: One seagrass plant in Shark Bay, Western Australia, has been found in meadows spanning at least 180 km, covering an estimated 200 km², about twice the size of Paris. We line up the biggest living things on Earth on real satellite images, to scale: the blue whale, a 47 m siphonophore, the Hyperion redwood, General Sherman, Pando (a forest that is one tree), the humongous honey fungus of Oregon, and the Shark Bay seagrass clone. Then the twist: a Baltic seaweed clone spread along more than 600 km of coast. So what counts as one living thing?
